simple.meaning: דּוּגָה (dûwgâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, fishery , i.e. a hook for fishing.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוּגָה (H1729) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דּוּגָה (H1729) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דּוּגָה (dûwgâh) / H1729 is traced through Amos 4:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, fishery , i.e. a hook for fishing
definitions.full: H1729. dugah דּוּגָה noun feminine fishing, fishery , only in דּוּגָה בְּסִירוֺת וְנִשָּׂא Amos 4:2 (|| בְּצִנּוֺת ) of ׳י , metaphor for dragging Israel captive (compare for practice referred to, in case of fish, Ezek 29:4 & Job 40:26 scornful summons to do it with crocodile, if possible ! see Herod ii. 70 on mode of capturing crocodiles ).
